question: Does the newly localized tool-learning integration seam beat the currently selected orchestration frontier on verified useful capability gain per wall-clock at $0 incremental spend?

proven_first_break.consumer_contract: reject discovery_source != APT_CATALOG and reject legacy score < 12

known_downstream_residuals: Full-metadata candidates currently emit matched_terms=[] while semantic verifier admission requires at least two matched terms.
Generic CLI contract inference remains intentionally narrow; prior PR56 did not close the parent capability because viable-candidate discovery was then upstream.

public_frontier_shape.toolathlon_verified: 108 verified long-horizon tasks across 32 applications / 604 tools; roughly 20 turns average; execution-based evaluators.
public_frontier_shape.peakbench: Executable multi-tool workflows with dependency annotations separate logical planning from resource-aware scheduling.
public_frontier_shape.frontier_provider_evidence: Current frontier providers explicitly evaluate or expose long-horizon multi-tool orchestration.

decision.rationale: The tool-learning seam is a real low-complexity defect but its first repair only restores pipeline access and immediately exposes at least one known downstream interface gate. The orchestration route is already implemented and individually evidenced; one unchanged fresh compound-DAG execution can produce a bounded verified obsolescence win or a first causal failure. This offers greater near-term verified capability gain per wall-clock.
automatic_reopen_conditions: Recompute immediately after the fresh orchestration gate reaches any terminal result.
Recompute immediately if the orchestration gate cannot obtain one verified zero-spend execution surface after one infrastructure attempt.
Reopen tool learning if real orchestration work is blocked by dynamic tool acquisition.
